header: Nifty PSU Sector Analysis (PSU Banks & PSE): 01Jul26 to 31Jul26
concise_summary: Nifty PSU Bank rallied on strong Q1 results
PNB profit surged sharply, aided by tax benefit
Canara Bank, Bank of India also posted strong Q1
Coal India profit flat, missed Street expectations
BEL fell despite strong revenue on margin miss
NTPC posted double-digit profit growth in Q1
US-Iran tensions kept PSU energy names volatile
Nifty Energy, PSU Bank dipped late in July
Defence and power PSUs saw a mixed results season
Broader PSU space stayed a key earnings-season focus
sector_news_last_month: Nifty PSU Bank rallied through much of July as Q1 FY27 (April-June 2026) results from major public-sector lenders came in better than expected
Punjab National Bank's results were a standout catalyst, with a very sharp year-on-year jump in net profit aided partly by a tax-related benefit alongside continued net interest income growth
Canara Bank and Union Bank of India also posted solid quarterly numbers, supporting a broad rally across PSU bank stocks around results day
Bank of India later reported strong profit growth alongside improving asset-quality metrics, with both gross and net non-performing-asset ratios easing sequentially
Private bank earnings during the same window were comparatively softer than PSU banks, reinforcing relative investor preference for public-sector lenders through the period
On the non-bank PSU side, Q1 FY27 earnings season also brought results from major power, energy, defence and mining companies

Coal India reported only a marginal rise in profit, with revenue growth offset by lower coal production and softer operating margins, and the stock declined on the results despite announcing an interim dividend
Bharat Electronics reported strong revenue growth but its stock fell as operating margins came in weaker than the market had expected
NTPC delivered double-digit profit growth for the quarter, continuing steady operational performance across its power-generation portfolio
Broader market volatility tied to the US-Iran conflict and swings in crude oil prices weighed intermittently on PSU energy names through the month

By the final week of July, some PSU segments cooled off alongside a broader bout of profit booking across sectoral indices, even as the underlying quarterly earnings trend for PSU banks remained largely positive
Government policy themes, including ongoing disinvestment and stake-monetisation plans, continued to be cited by analysts as a background sentiment factor across the PSU universe
